  - region "Simple English explanation of Vector Equation of a Plane":
    - paragraph: In simple English
    - heading "Understand Vector Equation of a Plane" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "A plane is n·(r−a)=0. With n=<0,0,1> and a=<0,0,3> this is z=3. The normal is perpendicular to every vector in the plane. A useful rule is Vector Equation of a Plane: r=a+su+tv. You can learn Vector Equation of a Plane by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: "Take a point on the plane and a normal, form n·(r−a)=0, then expand if Cartesian form is asked. Example: Name what s and t do in r=a+su+tv. u gives one direction. v gives another direction. So the answer is scale directions."
    - paragraph: "In real life, sheets: A flat surface has two directions. Watch out: Using parallel direction vectors for a plane. A plane needs two non-parallel directions."
    - complementary:
      - generic: Try this example
      - paragraph: Name what s and t do in r=a+su+tv.
      - generic "Compare your answer"
